stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

columns.label: Mean score on the final test (%)

rows.group: The group that took practice quizzes
The group that reread the passage

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that held the pen between the teeth
The group that held the pen between the lips

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They hypothesized that the number of other people present would affect the reporting of an emergency.

**Participants.** The sample was 80 university students, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

**Results.** The group that waited with four other people: mean time before reporting (s) = 196. The group that waited alone: mean time before reporting (s) = 58. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?**

**Source A.** In a study of 350 adults, the number of stressful life events in the past year correlated with the number of colds in that year (r = +0.33). Adults who reported sleeping less tended to report both more stress and more colds.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 84 office workers were randomly assigned to practice mindfulness meditation or to listen to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day. After eight weeks, the meditation group had a mean cortisol level of 9.8 nmol/L and the audiobook group 13.5 nmol/L (p = 0.02).

**Source C.** Researchers followed 500 people for a year after a major flood. Those who reported strong support from family and friends had fewer symptoms of illness and depression than those who reported little support.

questions.stem: In a drug trial, the patients do not know whether they are receiving the drug or a sugar pill, but the doctors do. Which procedure is this?

options.why: The control group is the group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison.
Statistical significance is the conclusion that a result is unlikely to have occurred by chance, usually when p is below 0.05.
A double-blind procedure is a procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition.
Correct. A single-blind procedure is a procedure in which the participants do not know which condition they are in.

questions.explanation: A single-blind procedure is a procedure in which the participants do not know which condition they are in.

questions.stem: A therapist asks her client to relax and say every thought that enters his head, however trivial or embarrassing. Which technique is this?

options.why: Correct. Free association is the psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind.
Active listening is the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says.
Dream interpretation is the psychodynamic technique of analyzing dreams to uncover unconscious wishes and conflicts.
Hypnosis is a state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories.

questions.explanation: Free association is the psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug?

options.why: A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.
An agonist is a drug that increases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by mimicking it.
An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.
Correct. Withdrawal is the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug.

questions.explanation: Withdrawal is the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: While counting basketball passes in a video, half of the viewers fail to see a person in a gorilla suit walk through the game. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.
Bottom-up processing is perception that starts with the raw sensory input and builds up to a complete picture.
Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.
Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.

questions.explanation: Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray?

options.why: Blindsight is the ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it.
Correct. Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.
The trichromatic theory is the theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue.
Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.

questions.explanation: Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.stem: On a dark night, Kai can make out shapes but not colors. Which receptor cells is he relying on?

options.why: The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.
The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.
Correct. Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.
The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.

questions.explanation: Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.

questions.stem: Researchers find that answers to questions about being talkative, sociable and outgoing all rise and fall together, which suggests a single trait. Which statistical method reveals such clusters?

options.why: Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.
A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.
Correct. Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.
Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.explanation: Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.

questions.stem: At age four, Noah learns to hold a pencil correctly and to fasten buttons. These are examples of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Fine motor skills is the movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt.
A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.
The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.
The rooting reflex is a newborn's automatic turning of the head toward a touch on the cheek, to find food.

questions.explanation: Fine motor skills is the movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder. What does this most limit?

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: A sleeper's EEG shows large, slow delta waves, and she is very difficult to wake. Which stage of sleep is she in?

options.why: NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.
REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.
The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.
Correct. NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.

questions.explanation: NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The number of years since leaving school
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

options.text: Score on a timed reasoning test
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: A doctor prescribes a fast-acting drug that calms a patient's panic by slowing central nervous system activity, warning that it can cause dependence. Which kind of drug is this?

options.why: Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.
Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.
Correct. An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.

questions.explanation: An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.

questions.stem: Although she was not listening, Bea can repeat the last few words her teacher just said. Which kind of memory makes this possible?

options.why: Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.
Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.
Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.
Correct. Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.

questions.explanation: Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that working memory span causes a change in reading comprehension score?

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Tess remembers the number 177618652001 by treating it as three famous years. Which technique is she using?

options.why: Correct. Chunking is the organizing of items into familiar, manageable units.
A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.
A mnemonic device is a memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks.
The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.

questions.explanation: Chunking is the organizing of items into familiar, manageable units.

questions.stem: Leo believes smoking is dangerous but smokes anyway; to reduce his discomfort, he decides the risks are exaggerated. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.
Correct. Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.
Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.

questions.explanation: Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes negative punishment?

options.text: The strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it
options.why: That describes negative reinforcement.

options.text: The weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it
options.why: Correct. This is what negative punishment means.

options.text: The weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it
options.why: That describes positive punishment.

options.text: The strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it
options.why: That describes positive reinforcement.

questions.explanation: Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the pituitary gland?

options.text: The structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning
options.why: That describes the cerebellum.

options.text: The network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness
options.why: That describes the reticular activating system.

options.text: The master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus
options.why: Correct. This is what the pituitary gland means.

options.text: The brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex
options.why: That describes the thalamus.

questions.explanation: The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.

questions.stem: In elevators, people face the door and avoid staring at strangers, although no law requires it. This unwritten rule is an example of which of the following?

options.why: The halo effect is the tendency for one good quality of a person to make us assume they have other good qualities.
The peripheral route to persuasion is persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker.
Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.
Correct. A social norm is a rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group.

questions.explanation: A social norm is a rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group.

questions.stem: After effective drugs were introduced, large numbers of patients were released from psychiatric hospitals to live in the community. What is this change called?

options.why: The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.
Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.
Correct. Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.explanation: Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.stem: A stranger risks her life to pull a child out of a river and expects nothing in return. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.
An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.
Correct. Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.

questions.explanation: Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes epigenetics?

options.text: Research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity
options.why: That describes a twin study.

options.text: The study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself
options.why: Correct. This is what epigenetics means.

options.text: The discredited movement that misused ideas about heredity to argue for selective breeding of humans
options.why: That describes eugenics.

options.text: The influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes
options.why: That describes nurture.

questions.explanation: Epigenetics is the study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself.

questions.stem: A researcher records how many hours of sleep 200 students get and their test scores, then checks whether the two are related. Which research method is this?

options.why: Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.
Naturalistic observation is the research method of watching and recording behavior in its natural setting without interfering.
Correct. A correlational study is the research method that measures two variables to see how they are related, without manipulating either.
A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.

questions.explanation: A correlational study is the research method that measures two variables to see how they are related, without manipulating either.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: A case study examines one individual in depth.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

options.text: The group that received no special response
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Several times a month and without warning, Jo's heart pounds, he cannot breathe and he feels he is dying; the episode passes in minutes. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Taijin kyofusho is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others.
Correct. Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.
Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Generalized anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person feels tense and worried most of the time about many things, for at least six months.

questions.explanation: Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced?

options.why: A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.
Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.
A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.
Correct. A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.

questions.explanation: A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.

questions.stem: Antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.
Correct. Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.

questions.explanation: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.

questions.stem: After a poor exam result, Bea feels better when she thinks about classmates who scored lower. Which process is this?

options.why: A dispositional attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to the person's own traits or character.
Correct. Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.
A situational attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances.

questions.explanation: Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a positive symptom?

options.text: The sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely
options.why: That describes an acute onset.

options.text: A symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations
options.why: Correct. This is what a positive symptom means.

options.text: A symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation
options.why: That describes a negative symptom.

options.text: The slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely
options.why: That describes a chronic course.

questions.explanation: A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.

questions.stem: People from an isolated culture correctly identify the emotions on the faces of people from a very different culture. This finding supports the existence of which of the following?

options.why: Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.
A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.
An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.
Correct. Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.

questions.explanation: Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: The highest score on a test is 98 and the lowest is 41, giving a value of 57. Which statistic is this?

options.why: The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of scores.
The median is the middle score when the scores are placed in order.
Correct. The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.
A percentile rank is the percentage of scores in a distribution that fall at or below a given score.

questions.explanation: The range is the difference between the highest and lowest scores.

questions.stem: After brain surgery, a patient remembers his past but forgets each new person minutes after meeting them. Which condition does he have?

options.why: Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.
Correct. Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.
Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.

questions.explanation: Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the somatosensory cortex?

options.text: The strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations
options.why: Correct. This is what the somatosensory cortex means.

options.text: The lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement
options.why: That describes the frontal lobes.

options.text: The strip at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements
options.why: That describes the motor cortex.

options.text: The lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language
options.why: That describes the temporal lobes.

questions.explanation: The somatosensory cortex is the strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the biopsychosocial model?

options.text: The view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors
options.why: Correct. This is what the biopsychosocial model means.

options.text: The use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem
options.why: That describes an eclectic approach.

options.text: The presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time
options.why: That describes comorbidity.

options.text: The view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience
options.why: That describes the diathesis-stress model.

questions.explanation: The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.

questions.stem: At twenty-two, Tariq has finished school but still lives with his parents and is exploring career options. Which period of life is he in?

options.why: The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.
The personal fable is the belief of adolescents that they are unique and that bad things will not happen to them.
Adverse childhood experiences is the stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect, that raise the risk of later problems.
Correct. Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.

questions.explanation: Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.

questions.stem: In which structure of the inner ear do hair cells convert sound vibrations into neural signals?

options.why: Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
Correct. The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.
Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.
Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.

questions.explanation: The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes transcendence?

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes love, kindness and social intelligence
options.why: That describes humanity.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty
options.why: Correct. This is what transcendence means.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control
options.why: That describes temperance.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning
options.why: That describes wisdom.

questions.explanation: Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.
Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: A committee refuses to approve a study that would cause participants severe distress. Which ethical requirement is the committee enforcing?

options.why: Correct. Protection from harm is the requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible.
Confidentiality is the keeping private of participants' identities and data.
Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.
Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.

questions.explanation: Protection from harm is the requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible.

questions.stem: To choose 500 students for a survey, a researcher uses a computer to pick names from the list of all students in the country. Which procedure is this?

options.why: Random assignment is the placing of participants in experimental conditions by chance.
Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.
A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.
Correct. Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.

questions.explanation: Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.

questions.stem: Rex looks for excitement through wild parties and reckless, uninhibited behavior. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Correct. Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.

questions.explanation: Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the primacy effect?

options.text: The finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together
options.why: That describes the spacing effect.

options.text: The tendency to remember the first items in a list well
options.why: Correct. This is what the primacy effect means.

options.text: The tendency to remember the last items in a list well
options.why: That describes the recency effect.

options.text: The tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones
options.why: That describes the serial position effect.

questions.explanation: The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.

questions.stem: A logo is made of three separate curved lines, but people see a complete circle. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.
Correct. Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.

questions.explanation: Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life?

options.why: Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Correct. Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.

questions.explanation: Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.

questions.stem: Ben is tormented by constant worry and feels miserable most of the day. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.
Correct. Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.
Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.

questions.explanation: Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate negative correlation appears as a band of points sloping downward.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: That would show a positive correlation.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

questions.explanation: A moderate negative correlation appears as a band of points sloping downward.

questions.stem: In Pavlov's experiments, dogs salivated to food, and later to a tone that had been paired with food. Salivating to the food was which of the following?

options.why: The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
Correct. The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.explanation: The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group that talked on the phone
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

options.text: The group that drove without a phone
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: A three-year-old says 'I runned fast' and 'two foots'. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.
Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.
Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.
Correct. Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.

questions.explanation: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The number of stressful life events in the past year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

options.text: The number of colds in the past year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Worried about a low grade that cannot be changed, Deb goes for a run and talks to a friend to feel calmer. Which kind of coping is this?

options.why: Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Correct. Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.

questions.explanation: Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as learning by watching others and imitating them?

options.why: Correct. Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.
Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.
Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.
A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.

questions.explanation: Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.

questions.stem: Kim knows that Paris is the capital of France, although she cannot remember when she learned it. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.
Correct. Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.

questions.explanation: Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises?

options.why: Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.
Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.
Correct. Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

questions.explanation: Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

questions.stem: People who move next to a railway are woken by trains at first but soon sleep through the noise. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.
One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.
Correct. Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.
Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.

questions.explanation: Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.

questions.stem: Wearing masks in a large, excited crowd, normally law-abiding fans begin smashing windows. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.
Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.
Correct. Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.explanation: Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading?

options.why: Recall is the retrieval of information without any cues, as in an essay question.
Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.
A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.
Correct. The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.

questions.explanation: The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a growth mindset?

options.text: The worry about confirming a negative stereotype about one's group, which can lower performance
options.why: That describes stereotype threat.

options.text: The belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed
options.why: That describes a fixed mindset.

options.text: The belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning
options.why: Correct. This is what a growth mindset means.

options.text: A test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future
options.why: That describes an aptitude test.

questions.explanation: A growth mindset is the belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning.

questions.stem: A female moth releases a chemical into the air that attracts males from far away. What is this chemical called?

options.why: Correct. A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.
Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.

questions.explanation: A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the misinformation effect?

options.text: The distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event
options.why: Correct. This is what the misinformation effect means.

options.text: The inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned
options.why: That describes source amnesia.

options.text: The increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it
options.why: That describes imagination inflation.

options.text: The building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information
options.why: That describes constructive memory.

questions.explanation: The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes synesthesia?

options.text: The conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses
options.why: That describes transduction.

options.text: The principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed
options.why: That describes Weber's law.

options.text: The smallest difference between two stimuli that a person can detect half of the time
options.why: That describes the just-noticeable difference.

options.text: The condition in which stimulating one sense produces an experience in another sense
options.why: Correct. This is what synesthesia means.

questions.explanation: Synesthesia is the condition in which stimulating one sense produces an experience in another sense.

questions.stem: Ice cream sales and drownings rise together, but both are caused by hot weather. Which problem does this illustrate?

options.why: A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
Correct. The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.

questions.explanation: The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain?

options.why: Correct. The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.

questions.explanation: The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the fundamental attribution error?

options.text: The feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with
options.why: That describes relative deprivation.

options.text: The tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits
options.why: That describes the actor-observer bias.

options.text: The tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation
options.why: Correct. This is what the fundamental attribution error means.

options.text: The habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors
options.why: That describes an optimistic explanatory style.

questions.explanation: The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.

questions.stem: Although Nell has handled coins thousands of times, she cannot say which way the head faces, because she never paid attention to it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.
Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.
Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.
Correct. Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.stem: A tourist calls another country's eating customs 'wrong' because they differ from the customs at home. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
Correct. Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes neuroplasticity?

options.text: The condition in which the two hemispheres cannot communicate because the corpus callosum has been cut
options.why: That describes a split brain.

options.text: The brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience
options.why: Correct. This is what neuroplasticity means.

options.text: An in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage
options.why: That describes a case study.

options.text: The destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function
options.why: That describes lesioning.

questions.explanation: Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience.

questions.stem: A client with borderline personality disorder learns mindfulness, ways of tolerating distress and ways of regulating emotions. Which therapy is this?

options.why: Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.
Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.
The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Correct. Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.

questions.explanation: Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of the reporting of an emergency

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of the reporting of an emergency.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: The reporting of an emergency was defined as the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The participants who were with other people took longer to report the smoke. On average, the value was 196 for the group that waited with four other people and 58 for the group that waited alone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 80 university students from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The participants who were with other people took longer to report the smoke. (196 compared with 58).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the number of other people present affects the reporting of an emergency. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the number of other people present. The finding illustrates the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility: people feel less personal duty to act when others are present.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Long-term stress harms health, but coping strategies and social support reduce its effects.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, people with more stressful life events had more colds in the same year (r = +0.33).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the general adaptation syndrome: prolonged stress keeps the body in the resistance phase and eventually exhausts it, which suppresses the immune system and makes illness more likely.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, workers who practiced mindfulness meditation had lower cortisol levels (9.8) than workers who listened to an audiobook (13.5).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through emotion-focused coping: meditation manages the emotional and physical reaction to stress, which lowers the body's stress-hormone response.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
